dict.string:
Captain Polliwog 0.3 (alpha)
The JavaScript engine is on. This build turns on the PowerPC baseline JIT, which had been built but not shipped. JavaScript is about twice as fast as before, and up to five times on the kind of code a charting library writes.
Faster everywhere else too. A fix to our copy of GCC removed a dead register save and restore from 15,928 of WebCore's functions. WebCore now exports 6,917 symbols instead of 73,627, which removed 5,484 stubs that stood in front of calls it makes to itself. Speedometer 3.1 on a PowerBook G4: 0.520, from 0.271 two days ago.
Video can be handed to a real player. QuickTime's H.264 decoder is the slowest part of watching anything on these machines. Right-click a video, use the green button on it, the View menu or the Share menu, and it opens in VLC or MPlayer instead, which decode with AltiVec. The stream goes through the browser's own networking, so seeking works and sites that refuse Tiger's TLS are reachable.
Full screen works. It was off twice over: WebKit's own preference for it, and the missing unprefixed requestFullscreen() that modern players look for.
Nothing plays by itself. A video that starts on its own is the whole processor on a G4. Pages that call play() from script are now stopped until you ask. Preferences has a switch for it.
Say when something is wrong. There is a Send Feedback window now, and an About window that says what this is and which build you are on.
Known: Charts-chartjs is still slower than PowerFox. There is no Media Source Extensions, so YouTube will only offer 360p. Tiger and G3 support is not in this build.

Captain Polliwog 0.3.1 (alpha)
Welcome aboard. The first time it opens, the Captain introduces himself and offers to bring your Safari bookmarks across, to become your default browser, and to recommend a media player. The video page only recommends VLC on a Mac that can run it - its PowerPC build needs AltiVec, which a G3 does not have - and says so honestly on one that cannot. You can finish it later: untick "Don't show this again". Preferences > General has Run Setup Again.
Scrolling speed. Preferences > General > Scrolling: Slow, Medium, Fast or Very fast. Slow is the new default. The trackpad on these PowerBooks reports its own accelerated movement, and the old setting was moving pages more than a screen and a half a second.
Check for Updates says what it means. "Up to date" is now a plain answer with the version and build, instead of a window with an empty box in it and a progress bar running under its buttons.
The About window. The Cytrus Software logo is the real one now, and the icons are the right way up.
Known: Charts-chartjs is still slower than PowerFox. There is no Media Source Extensions, so YouTube only offers 360p - use the green Play in VLC button for a smoother picture. Tiger and G3 support is not in this build.
